evidence: Verg. Ecl. 8.80: haec ut cēra liquēscit
Plin. NH 28.144: sēvum liquefierī prius jubent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Mostly in the passive, liquefierī; the active is rare (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: «Liquēscetne illa nix, tata?» «In summīs montibus nē aestāte quidem liquēscit.»
phrases.english: “Will that snow melt, Dad?” “On the highest mountains it doesn’t melt even in summer.”
phrases.source: Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

phrases.latin: Būtȳrum in patellā pōne, et sine lēniter liquēscat.
phrases.english: Put the butter in the pan and let it melt gently.

sources: Lewis & Short: liquesco · Lewis & Short: liquefacio
